correctness.rationale: A standalone Python 3 verifier reconstructs the 21 incidence edges, exhausts all 3462 augmented simplices, performs exact mod-two boundary reduction with ranks (20,148,496,722,312,24), and proves rational homology concentrated in degree four with rank 16 using the Euler characteristic. It enumerates all 168 group matrices, directly computes every oriented fixed-face Lefschetz trace, checks against an independent signed orbit-polynomial formula, constructs eight Sylow-7 subgroups and their conjugation action, and verifies all character orthogonality and rational semisimplicity identities. Both formulations agree at all 168 elements; assumptions, signs and empty-face normalization were checked.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object public Heawood result explicitly claims no equivariant statement; it supplies only the 16-dimensional homotopy rank. Full text of Bate–Everitt–Ford–Ramos deals with complete-hypergraph S_n actions, rather than the Fano incidence graph or GL(3,2) multiplicities. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches for Heawood/Fano/Levi automorphism representations, order-7 traces, and aliases returned no exact representation. The new claim adds complete fixed-face traces and a nonobvious 1+7+8 decomposition; generic character tables do not imply which constituents occur. Residual indexing/priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The Fano plane carries a canonical highly transitive automorphism group, so its action on matching-complex homology is a natural structural invariant. Decomposition into three distinct irreducibles of dimensions 1,7,8 (including a genuine invariant line) identifies symmetry information invisible to the known nonequivariant wedge of sixteen spheres. The complete 168-element calculation and Sylow-7 geometric model are useful as exact equivariant benchmarks, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no larger-family theorem is asserted.
